- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment periods (model lags or underreacts to bearish signals).
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term volatility; smooth out sharp spikes in forecasted price movements.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often delays correction — adjust forecast downward slightly to reflect sentiment lag.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been trending sharply upward, model tends to overpredict further gains — reduce forecast slope after 3+ consecutive upward moves.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often overestimates later periods (especially 20-30d) — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for final 5–10 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated positive spikes followed by negative corrections, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast peak by 1–2% after 2+ consecutive positive sentiment days.
